source_text: Ὀπὴν οὖν τινα ὀλίγην ὑποδείξαντες »τοῖς φιλοθεάμοσι τῆς ἀληθείας« ἐκ τοῦ κατὰ τὰς θυσίας νόμου περί τε Ἰουδαίων τῶν χυδαίων περί τε τῶν αἱρέσεων μυστικῶς διακρινομένων. ὡς ἀκαθάρτων, ἀπὸ τῆς [περὶ καθαρῶν καὶ ἀκαθάρτων ζῴων] θείας ἐκκλησίας, καταπαύσωμεν τὸν λόγον. τὰ μὲν γὰρ διχηλοῦντα καὶ μηρυκισμὸν ἀνάγοντα τῶν ἱερείων καθαρὰ καὶ δεκτὰ τῷ θεῷ παραδίδωσιν ἡ γραφή, ὡς ἂν εἰς πατέρα καὶ εἰς υἱὸν διὰ τῆς πίστεως τῶν δικαίων τὴν πορείαν ποιουμένων (αὕτη γὰρ ἡ τῶν διχηλούντων ἑδραιότης) τῶν »τὰ λόγια τοῦ θεοῦ« »νύκτωρ καὶ μεθ᾿ ἡμέραν μελετώντων« καὶ ἀναπεμπαζομένων ἐν τῷ τῆς ψυχῆς τῶν μαθημάτων δοχείῳ. ἣν * καὶ συνάσκησιν γνωστικὴν ὑπάρχουσαν καθαροῦ ζῴου μηρυκισμὸν ὁ νόμος ἀλληγορεῖ. ὅσα δὲ μήτε ἑκάτερον μήτε τὸ ἕτερον τούτων ἔχει, ὡς ἀκάθαρτα ἀφορίζει. αὐτίκα τὰ ἀνάγοντα μηρυκισμόν, μὴ διχηλοῦντα δέ. τοὺς Ἰουδαίους αἰνίσσεται τοὺς πολλούς, οἳ τὰ μὲν λόγια τοῦ θεοῦ ἀνὰ στόμα ἔχουσιν. τὴν δὲ πίστιν καὶ τὴν βάσιν δι᾿ υἱοῦ πρὸς τὸν πατέρα παραπέμπουσαν οὐκ ἔχουσιν ἐπερειδομένην τῇ ἀληθείᾳ. ὅθεν καὶ ὀλισθηρὸν τὸ γένος τῶν τοιούτων θρεμμάτων, ὡς ἂν μὴ σχιδανοπόδων ὄντων μηδὲ τῇ διπλόῃ τῆς πίστεως ἐπερειδομένων· »οὐδεὶς γάρ«. φησί, »γινώσκει τὸν πατέρα εἰ μὴ ὁ υἱὸς καὶ ᾧ ἂν ὁ υἱὸς ἀποκαλύψῃ.« ἔμπαλίν τε αὖ ἀκάθαρτα ὁμοίως κἀκεῖνα. ὅσα διχηλεῖ μέν. μηρυκισμὸν δὲ οὐκ ἀνάγει. ταυτὶ γὰρ τοὺς αἱρετικοὺς ἐνδείκνυται ὀνόματι μὲν πατρὸς καὶ υἱοῦ ἐπιβεβηκότας. τὴν δὲ τῶν λογίων ἀκριβῆ σαφήνειαν λεπτουργεῖν καὶ καταλεαίνειν ἐξασθενοῦντας, πρὸς δὲ καὶ τὰ ἔργα τῆς δικαιοσύνης ὁλοσχερέστερον. οὐχὶ δὲ ἀκριβέστερον μετερχομένους, εἴ γε καὶ μετέλθοιεν. τοιούτοις τισὶν ὁ κύριος λέγει· »τί με λέγετε ›κύριε κύριε‹ καὶ οὐ ποιεῖτε ἃ λέγω;« ἀκάθαρτοι δὲ πάμπαν οἱ μὴ διχηλοῦντες μηδὲ ἀνάγοντες μηρυκισμόν. ὑμεῖς δ᾿, ὦ Μεγαρεῖς, φησὶν ὁ Φέογνις, οὔτε τρίτοι οὔτε τέταρτοι οὔτε δυωδέκατοι οὔτ᾿ ἐν λόγῳ οὔτ᾿ ἐν ἀριθμῷ, »ἀλλ᾿ ἢ ὡς ὁ χνοῦς, ὃν ἐκρίπτει ὁ ἄνεμος ἀπὸ προσώπου τῆς γῆς« καὶ »ὡς σταγὼν ἀπὸ κάδου«. Τούτων ἡμῖν προδιηνυσμένων καὶ τοῦ ἠθικοῦ τόπου ὡς ἐν κεφαλαίῳ ὑπογραφέντος, σποράδην, ὡς ὑπεσχήμεθα, καὶ διερριμμένως τὰ ζώπυρα τῶν τῆς ἀληθοῦς γνώσεως ἐγκατασπείραντες δογμάτων, ὡς μὴ ῥᾳδίαν εἶναι τῷ περιτυχόντι τῶν ἀμυήτων τὴν τῶν ἁγίων παραδόσεων εὕρεσιν, μετίωμεν ἐπὶ τὴν ὑπόσχεσιν. ἐοίκασι δέ πως οἱ Στρωματεῖς οὐ παραδείσοις ἐξησκημένοις ἐκείνοις τοῖς ἐν στοίχῳ καταπεφυτευμένοις εἰς ἡδονὴν ὄψεως. ὄρει δὲ μᾶλλον συσκίῳ τινὶ καὶ δασεῖ κυπαρίσσοις καὶ πλατάνοις δάφνῃ τε καὶ κισσῷ, μηλέαις τε ὁμοῦ καὶ ἐλαίαις καὶ συκαῖς καταπεφυτευμένῳ, ἐξεπίτηδες ἀναμεμιγμένης τῆς φυτείας καρποφόρων τε ὁμοῦ καὶ ἀκάρπων δένδρων διὰ τοὺς ὑφαιρεῖσθαι καὶ κλέπτειν τολμῶντας τὰ ὥρια, ἐθελούσης λανθάνειν τῆς γραφῆς. ἐξ ὧν δὴ μεταμοσχεύσας καὶ μεταφυτεύσας ὁ γεωργὸς ὡραῖον κατακοσμήσει παράδεισον καὶ ἄλσος ἐπιτερπές. οὔτ᾿ οὖν τῆς τάξεως οὔτε τῆς φράσεως στοχάζονται οἱ Στρωματεῖς, ὅπου γε ἐπίτηδες καὶ τὴν λέξιν οὐχ Ἕλληνες εἶναι βούλονται καὶ τὴν τῶν δογμάτων ἐγκατασπορὰν λεληθότως καὶ οὐ κατὰ τὴν ἀλήθειαν πεποίηνται, φιλοπόνους καὶ εὑρετικοὺς εἶναι τοὺς ἀναγιγνώσκοντας> εἴ τινες τύχοιεν παρασκευάζοντες. πολλὰ γὰρ τὰ δελέατα καὶ ποικίλα διὰ τὰς τῶν ἰχθύων διαφοράς. Καὶ δὴ μετὰ τὸν ἕβδομον τοῦτον ἡμῖν Στρωματέα τῶν ἑξῆς ἀπ᾿ ἄλλης ἀρχῆς ποιησόμεθα τὸν λόγον.
pass_a_gloss: Having shown a certain small thing to those who love to behold the truth, from the law concerning the sacrifices, concerning both the Jews of the crowd and the mystical distinctions of the heresies, let us stop the discourse, as from the divine church of the pure and impure animals. For the scripture hands over the pure and acceptable things to God, which both divide the hoof and bring up the cud, of the priests, as if making a journey to the Father and to the Son through the faith of the righteous, (for this is the stability of those who divide the hoof) of those who meditate on the words of God night and day and are sent forth in the vessel of the soul's teachings. Which also the law allegorizes as the exercise of a pure animal, bringing up the cud. But as many as have neither this nor that, it separates as impure. Immediately, those that bring up the cud, not dividing the hoof. It accuses the many Jews, who have the words of God in their mouth, but do not have the faith and the foundation through the Son to the Father, having been deceived by the truth. Whence also the race of such people is slippery, as if they were not cloven-hoofed nor having the double tunic of faith; for no one, it says, knows the Father except the Son and to whom the Son reveals. And in turn, equally impure are those that divide the hoof but do not bring up the cud. For these indicate the heretics, who have come upon the name of Father and Son, but undermine and destroy the precise clarity of the words, and also the works of righteousness, not going more accurately, even if they were to go. To such people the Lord says: Why do you call me 'Lord, Lord' and do not do what I say? But those that neither divide the hoof nor bring up the cud are completely impure. You, however, Megarians, says Theognis, are neither third nor fourth nor twelfth, neither in word nor in number, but like the dust that the wind blows away from the face of the earth and like a drop from a bucket. Having gone through these things and the ethical topic, as if in a chapter, having sown the seeds of the true knowledge, as we promised, and having scattered them, that it is not easy for the one who happens upon the unwritten traditions of the saints to find them, let us proceed to the promise. The Stromata seem to be not like gardens exercised by those who have been planted in a row for the pleasure of sight. But rather like a mountain, shady and dense with cypresses and planes, laurel and ivy, apples and olives and figs, planted together, with the planting of fruit-bearing and barren trees mixed intentionally, because of those who dare to steal and snatch the timely things, the scripture wanting to hide. From which the farmer, having grafted and transplanted, will beautifully adorn a paradise and a pleasant grove. Therefore, the Stromata do not consider either the order or the phrase, since they intentionally do not want to be Greek even in language, and they have made the sowing of the doctrines secretly and not according to the truth, to be laborious and inventive for those who read, if any happen to be preparing. For there are many things that are obscure and varied, because of the differences of the fish. And so, after this seventh Stromata, we will make the discourse from another beginning.

pass_b_english: Having shown a small glimpse to those who love to behold the truth, drawn from the law concerning sacrifices — a passage that mystically distinguishes both the common Jews and the heresies as unclean, removing them from the divine church of clean and unclean animals — let us stop our discourse here. Scripture hands over to God the animals that are clean and acceptable, those that both divide the hoof and chew the cud; these represent the priests who make their way to the Father and to the Son through the faith of the righteous — for this stability belongs to those who divide the hoof — those who meditate on the words of God night and day and are sent forth in the vessel of the soul's teachings. The law allegorizes this practice of a clean animal chewing the cud as a spiritual exercise. But those that have neither characteristic, or only one, it sets apart as unclean. First, those that chew the cud but do not divide the hoof: these signify the many Jews who have the words of God in their mouths, yet lack the faith and the foundation that leads through the Son to the Father, a foundation fixed upon the truth. Hence the race of such creatures is slippery, as though they were not cloven-hoofed nor supported by the double garment of faith; for, "no one knows the Father except the Son and anyone to whom the Son chooses to reveal him" (Matt 11:27). In turn, equally unclean are those that divide the hoof but do not chew the cud. These point to the heretics, who have laid hold of the name of Father and Son, yet weaken and wear away the precise clarity of the divine words, and also the works of righteousness, not advancing more accurately even if they do advance at all. To such people the Lord says, "Why do you call me 'Lord, Lord,' and not do what I tell you?" (Luke 6:46). But those that neither divide the hoof nor chew the cud are completely unclean. "You, however, Megarians," says Theognis, "are neither third nor fourth nor twelfth, neither in word nor in number, but like the dust that the wind blows away from the face of the earth and like a drop from a bucket."

Having gone through these matters and sketched the ethical topic as in a summary, and having sown the seeds of the true knowledge here and there, scattered as we promised, so that it would not be easy for the chance reader among the uninitiated to find the unwritten traditions of the saints, let us proceed to the promise. The Stromata do not resemble gardens carefully laid out with plants set in rows for the pleasure of the eye. Rather, they are like a mountain, shady and thick with cypresses and planes, laurel and ivy, apples and olives and figs planted together, with fruit-bearing and barren trees intentionally intermingled because of those who dare to steal and snatch the ripe fruit, the Scripture itself willing to remain hidden. From this mixed planting the farmer, by grafting and transplanting, will fashion a beautiful paradise and a delightful grove. Therefore the Stromata pay attention neither to order nor to phrasing; indeed, they deliberately do not wish to be Greek even in language, and they have scattered the sowing of the doctrines covertly and not according to the obvious sense, so that those who read — if any happen to be preparing themselves — must be diligent and inventive. For there are many things obscure and varied, because of the differences among the fish. And so, after this seventh Stromata, we will begin the discourse anew from another starting point.

review.notes: The translation accurately captures the complex allegorical structure of the Greek text regarding the division of the hoof and the chewing of the cud. Pass A preserves the clause structure and nuances of the Greek, while Pass B provides the necessary scripture citations (Matthew 11:27 and Luke 6:46) for the quoted clauses, which is required by the rules. The title 'Purification of the Church' captures the thematic essence of the passage.
